english: how much; how long; how many
use: The everyday question for any amount, time or distance; dore kurai is the same word.

example.ja: 駅までどれぐらいかかる？
example.english: How long does it take to get to the station?

examplePolite.romaji: Eki made dore gurai kakarimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 駅までどれぐらいかかりますか？
examplePolite.english: How long does it take to get to the station?

notes: For a rough answer, put gurai after the number: juppun gurai (about ten minutes).

use: Usually emotional: how much someone worried, waited or cared, not a neutral measurement.

example.romaji: Dore dake shinpai shita to omotteru no?
example.ja: どれだけ心配したと思ってるの？
example.english: Do you know how worried I was?

examplePolite.romaji: Dore dake shinpai shita to omotte iru n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: どれだけ心配したと思っているんですか？
examplePolite.english: Do you have any idea how worried I was?

notes: For a plain question about amount or time, dore gurai is more usual.

use: Usually with -te mo: donna ni ganbatte mo (no matter how hard I try).

example.romaji: Donna ni isogashikute mo, asagohan wa taberu yo.
example.ja: どんなに忙しくても、朝ごはんは食べるよ。
example.english: No matter how busy I am, I eat breakfast.

examplePolite.romaji: Donna ni isogashikute mo, asagohan wa tabemasu.
examplePolite.ja: どんなに忙しくても、朝ごはんは食べます。
examplePolite.english: No matter how busy I am, I eat breakfast.

notes: Also in exclamations: donna ni ureshikatta ka (you can't imagine how happy I was).

english: what on earth; (who, why) on earth
use: Adds surprise or frustration to a question word: ittai nani, ittai dare, ittai doushite.

example.ja: いったい何があったの？
example.english: What on earth happened?

examplePolite.romaji: Ittai nani ga atta n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: いったい何があったんですか？
examplePolite.english: What on earth happened?

notes: Ittai zentai is an even stronger version.

use: A warmer, more emphatic totemo, common in friendly or gushing speech.

example.ja: このケーキ、とってもおいしい！
example.english: This cake is so good!

examplePolite.romaji: Kono keeki, tottemo oishii desu.
examplePolite.ja: このケーキ、とってもおいしいです。
examplePolite.english: This cake is really delicious.

notes: Plain totemo is the neutral form.

use: Informal intensifier before adjectives and verbs; on its own it means a mess or ruined.

example.ja: 昨日の試合、めちゃくちゃ面白かった。
example.english: Yesterday's game was super fun.

examplePolite.romaji: Kinou no shiai wa mechakucha omoshirokatta desu.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日の試合はめちゃくちゃ面白かったです。
examplePolite.english: Yesterday's game was really fun.

notes: Often shortened to mecha (mecha oishii). Heya ga mechakucha da = the room is a total mess.

use: Comments on a surprising amount or change: zuibun hayai ne, zuibun kawatta.

example.ja: 随分大きくなったね！
example.english: You've grown so much!

examplePolite.romaji: Zuibun ookiku narimashita ne.
examplePolite.ja: 随分大きくなりましたね。
examplePolite.english: He's grown so much.

notes: Can sound critical: zuibun na iikata da ne (that's a harsh thing to say).

use: Casual exaggeration with feelings and states: shinu hodo tsukareta, shinu hodo waratta.

example.ja: 今日は死ぬほど疲れた。
example.english: I'm dead tired today.

examplePolite.romaji: Kyou wa shinu hodo tsukaremashita.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は死ぬほど疲れました。
examplePolite.english: I'm exhausted today.

notes: Hodo after a verb means 'to the point of': naku hodo ureshii (so happy I could cry).

use: The reply to 'how was it?' when it was OK but not great.

example.ja: 試験どうだった？—まあまあかな。
example.english: How was the exam? — So-so, I guess.

examplePolite.romaji: Shiken wa dou deshita ka? — Maamaa deshita.
examplePolite.ja: 試験はどうでしたか？—まあまあでした。
examplePolite.english: How was the exam? — It was all right.

notes: Said softly to calm someone: maamaa, ochitsuite (now, now, calm down).

use: Neither bad nor great; often modest about your own skills or things.

example.ja: あの店、そこそこおいしいよ。
example.english: That place is pretty decent.

examplePolite.romaji: Ano mise wa sokosoko oishii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あの店はそこそこおいしいですよ。
examplePolite.english: That restaurant is fairly good.

notes: Sokosoko no = decent, okay-ish: sokosoko no kyuuryou (a decent salary).

english: reasonably; in its own way; as you'd expect
use: Usually sorenari ni: decent enough given the situation, effort or price.

example.romaji: Renshuu shita kara, sorenari ni dekita.
example.ja: 練習したから、それなりにできた。
example.english: I'd practiced, so it went reasonably well.

examplePolite.romaji: Renshuu shita node, sorenari ni dekimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 練習したので、それなりにできました。
examplePolite.english: I had practiced, so it went fairly well.

notes: Sorenari no = fitting, matching: sorenari no riyuu (a good enough reason).

english: to some extent; a certain amount
use: Hedges a claim so you don't overstate it.

example.romaji: Nihongo wa aru teido wakaru yo.
example.ja: 日本語はある程度わかるよ。
example.english: I understand Japanese to some extent.

examplePolite.romaji: Nihongo wa aru teido wakarimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 日本語はある程度わかります。
examplePolite.english: I understand Japanese to a certain degree.

notes: A bit more neutral and work-friendly than sokosoko.

use: Stronger than ima: it happened a moment ago.

example.ja: たった今着いたところ。
example.english: I literally just got here.

examplePolite.romaji: Tatta ima tsuita tokoro desu.
examplePolite.ja: たった今着いたところです。
examplePolite.english: I've just this moment arrived.

notes: Often with -ta tokoro (have just done): tatta ima deta tokoro (just left).

english: in no time; in the blink of an eye
use: For time flying or something happening fast, often with -te shimau.

example.romaji: Natsuyasumi, atto iu ma ni owatchatta ne.
example.ja: 夏休み、あっという間に終わっちゃったね。
example.english: Summer break was over in no time.

examplePolite.romaji: Natsuyasumi wa atto iu ma ni owatte shimaimashita ne.
examplePolite.ja: 夏休みはあっという間に終わってしまいましたね。
examplePolite.english: The summer holidays flew by.

notes: Atto iu ma datta = it flew by.

english: when did...?; before I knew it
use: Surprise that something happened without you noticing.

example.romaji: Itsu no ma ni kami kitta no?
example.ja: いつの間に髪切ったの？
example.english: When did you cut your hair?

examplePolite.romaji: Itsu no ma ni kami o kitta n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: いつの間に髪を切ったんですか？
examplePolite.english: When did you get your hair cut?

notes: Add ka for a statement: itsu no ma ni ka nete ita (I fell asleep before I knew it).

english: by the end of today; sometime today
use: Sets a deadline for today.

example.ja: 今日中に返事するね。
example.english: I'll get back to you by the end of today.

examplePolite.romaji: Kyoujuu ni ohenji shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今日中にお返事します。
examplePolite.english: I'll reply by the end of today.

notes: Same pattern for this week: konshuuchuu ni.

use: Things go, or should go, the normal way: itsumo doori de ii (the usual is fine).

example.ja: 今日もいつもどおり忙しかった。
example.english: Busy as usual today.

examplePolite.romaji: Kyou mo itsumo doori isogashikatta desu.
examplePolite.ja: 今日もいつもどおり忙しかったです。
examplePolite.english: Today was busy, as usual.

notes: -doori means 'just as': yotei doori (as planned).

use: A casual 'often', usually hinting 'too often'.

example.romaji: Kare, shotchuu chikoku suru yo ne.
example.ja: 彼、しょっちゅう遅刻するよね。
example.english: He's always late, isn't he?

examplePolite.romaji: Kare wa shotchuu chikoku shimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 彼はしょっちゅう遅刻しますね。
examplePolite.english: He's late all the time.

notes: More casual and stronger than yoku (often).

use: States the general rule while leaving room for exceptions.

example.romaji: Doyoubi wa kihonteki ni yasumi da yo.
example.ja: 土曜日は基本的に休みだよ。
example.english: I'm basically off on Saturdays.

examplePolite.romaji: Doyoubi wa kihonteki ni yasumi desu.
examplePolite.ja: 土曜日は基本的に休みです。
examplePolite.english: Saturdays are generally my day off.

notes: -teki ni makes adverbs from nouns: jikanteki ni (time-wise).

english: heart pounding; be nervous; be thrilled
use: A racing heart from nerves, excitement or a crush.

example.romaji: Happyou no mae, sugoi dokidoki shita.
example.ja: 発表の前、すごいドキドキした。
example.english: My heart was pounding before the presentation.

examplePolite.romaji: Happyou no mae wa totemo dokidoki shimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 発表の前はとてもドキドキしました。
examplePolite.english: I was really nervous before the presentation.

notes: Wakuwaku is pure happy excitement; dokidoki includes nerves.
